design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec.finding: The ADR/Phase0 matrix left this fully open ('This full shape is a Phase 0 deliverable, not frozen here'). Decision point 1/2 and evidence 0181 pin the dynamic resolver has NO _records slot and never caches artifact bytes -- but _p4_close_admission's own visit()/find() pattern (which this function mirrors 'the shape' of) resolves EVERY artifact, including the top-level admission_ref itself, through _P4_CHECKED_RESOLVE against a resolver-held records table. A resolver with no records table structurally cannot hold caller-supplied root-capture-admission/cas/pce bytes the way the legacy fixture_facts mechanism does (and Decision point 1 explicitly forbids fixture_facts on the dynamic resolver).
design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec.decision: _dynamic_p4_close_admission deterministically RECONSTRUCTS the expected root-capture-admission and cas documents from (a) the graph's own closed 12-reference set (root_pis_ref/dataset_g1_ref/dataset_g2_ref, each provably unique by kind/role) and (b) the live runtime/captures already gated by commit_p4_batch's own checks, rather than resolving them as independently stored artifacts. A caller-supplied admission_ref is admitted only if its digest matches this reconstruction exactly. This is what refuses an aliased/swapped/foreign admission_ref (matrix row 6) and makes a pce entry-swap (matrix row 7) structurally impossible rather than merely checked-for.
design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec.tradeoff_disclosed: This is a stricter, narrower reading than a literal 'stored and independently resolved artifact' interpretation might suggest. It satisfies every matrix row's expected_outcome and forbidden_effect as pinned, and is directly tested (test_adr143_matrix_row6_forged_admission_ref_refuses, test_adr143_matrix_row7_planned_entry_binding_is_recomputed_not_trusted, test_adr143_positive_close_admission_succeeds_for_a_real_captured_chain).

design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec.finding: Evidence 0181's class_function_inventory pinned a fresh `_P4_PENDING_DYNAMIC_TOKENS` set 'mirrors _P4_PENDING_TOKENS, never the legacy set.' This does not work: _SyntheticP4CapturedAuthorizationAuthority.__init__ is explicitly required to stay the EXISTING, UNMODIFIED class (Decision point 3), and its __init__ body hardcodes the literal check `if token not in _P4_PENDING_TOKENS`. A second, separate pending-token set can never satisfy that hardcoded check without editing __init__ itself, which Decision point 3 forbids ('no second... CapturedAuthorizationAuthority implementation'). Decision point 3's own prose elsewhere says the SAME _P4_PENDING_TOKENS discipline is reused, which is consistent with the code and inconsistent with the matrix's inventory annotation.
design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec.decision: _development_dynamic_p4_broker uses the shared, existing _P4_PENDING_TOKENS set (matching Decision point 3's literal text) for the authority construction step; only the resolver construction step uses its own new, dedicated _P4_PENDING_DYNAMIC_RESOLVER_TOKENS set (which is _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver's own new __init__, fully within this ADR's authority to design).

convergence_checkpoint.trigger: Genuine architectural contradiction discovered during GREEN, not resolvable by a 'smallest generic change' within this ADR's own stated constraints -- disclosed per docs/skills/skeptic-review.md's convergence rule instead of a fourth undisclosed patch attempt.
convergence_checkpoint.finding: The full authorize_capture_set -> CAPTURED path is blocked for the dynamic authority. Two independent, compounding reasons, both in SHARED code this ADR's Decision points 3 and 6 require to stay unedited for both authority instances: (1) _p4_checked_dispatch calls the module-level _p4_reference_bytes(admission_ref) unconditionally; that function's _P4_ADMISSION_SCHEMAS whitelist hardcodes only {'action-execution-admission', 'final-replay-admission'} and has no case for 'root-capture-admission', so it refuses before resolver.close_admission is ever reached (ValueError: 'P4 admission kind, role and schema must agree'). (2) Even if (1) is set aside, _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare (also shared/unedited per Decision point 6) reads resolver._records directly in multiple places and requires admission['plan_evaluation_authorization_sha256']/['capture_expectation_set_sha256']/['broker_verified_plan_sha256'] fields on ANY admission document routed through it -- fields the dynamic resolver's root-capture-admission/cas/pce chain (Decision point 7, which explicitly excludes pea/ces/bvp/scope machinery as a non-goal) structurally does not and must not have.
convergence_checkpoint.why_not_patched: Fixing (1) would require editing the shared _p4_reference_bytes whitelist or _p4_checked_dispatch itself -- functions ADR-0143 does not name as extensible (only _p4_require_issued_authority and _p4_snapshot_integrity are named). Fixing (2) would require either (a) giving the dynamic resolver a _records-like table after all, directly contradicting evidence 0181's explicit 'no _records slot' Phase 0 pin, or (b) extending _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract/_P4_PREPARE with resolver-type dispatch, contradicting Decision point 3's 'no second... implementation' and Decision point 6's 'remain shared, unedited' for the signing infrastructure, or (c) inventing synthetic pea/ces/bvp-shaped documents for the dynamic chain, which reintroduces exactly the legacy scope-intent/gate-evidence/scope-authorization/stage-admission apparatus this ADR's own Non-goals section forbids reusing. Every option contradicts an explicit ADR-0143 decision point or Phase 0 pin; none is a 'smallest generic change.' This is a genuine design gap in the accepted ADR text, not an implementation defect, and needs a fresh reviewed decision (a follow-on ADR), not a silent GREEN-time workaround.
convergence_checkpoint.what_was_delivered_instead: Everything the ADR actually specifies as novel and independently testable was implemented and is GREEN: the resolver/terminal/clock/revocations classes, the one-shot reserve-first construction with pins F1/F2/F3, the extended dispatch functions, and _dynamic_p4_close_admission itself (the ADR's own required fourth resolver method, exercised directly via resolver.close_admission(...) in test_adr143_positive_close_admission_succeeds_for_a_real_captured_chain, which drives a REAL F4 produce/seal/publish lifecycle twice and closes a genuine matching admission chain with zero effect, exactly as the ADR's nonauthorizing contract requires). test_adr143_authorize_capture_set_blocked_by_prepare_contract pins the disclosed refusal as a fact, not a silent gap.
convergence_checkpoint.recommendation: A follow-on ADR should decide, with fresh independent review, one of: extend _p4_checked_dispatch/_p4_reference_bytes and _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare with the SAME kind of exact-type if/elif/else dispatch this ADR already used successfully for _p4_require_issued_authority/_p4_snapshot_integrity; or give the dynamic resolver a minimal, closed, non-caller-selectable records-equivalent scoped only to its own 3-document chain plus a parallel, resolver-typed _prepare path. Both are larger and more trust-boundary-sensitive than this slice's stated scope, which is why they are deferred rather than improvised here.
